decisions.statement: Each line names a page and a key and the value put into that key.
The value is the rest of the line.
A line that is not a path and a key and a value parted by spaces is refused.
A line with nothing on it is read over.
A call handing in no line is refused.
A key naming a relation has its value resolved before any body is worked out.
A value naming no page is refused where the key names a relation.
A key naming no relation takes its value unresolved.
A path the world names no page at is refused.
Whether the property has one value is read from the type the page states.
A line is put in against the world the lines before it leave.
A refusal at any line refuses the whole call and names that line.
A call that refuses puts in no value at all.
Putting each value in is left to the mechanical change of the same name.
That change is reached through the runner rather than by an import.
Nothing here says where among a property's values a value lands.
Nothing here works out a body of its own.
A key the page writes nowhere yet is put in where the pages of its type write it.
`after` is left out where the pages of that type write the key nowhere.
A key the page's type declares no property for is refused.
That refusal names the record a field of a record is reached through.
A page whose type cannot be read has no key refused.
What a property holds is read from the type the page states.
A property holding a boolean or a number is handed on as holding it.
A refusal over a slug the page's type declares a key for names the key to write instead.

definition: many values put into the properties their lines name, in one call
